title: Little Office of B. Niccolo Albergati

introductoryNotes.text: From a book of the same name published in 1746.

translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto, Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Magni Patris magnae Proli, E Brunonis caelo Soli Lingua laudes resonat, Dulce melos intonat.
blocks.english: To the great offspring of a great father, a sun from Bruno’s heaven, the tongue sounds praises and intones a sweet melody.

blocks.source: Nicolai Albergati, Caeli Civis ter Beati, Celebra memoriam, Meditare gloriam.
blocks.english: Celebrate the memory of Nicholas Albergati, thrice-blessed citizen of heaven; meditate upon his glory.

blocks.source: Candicantem puritatem, Purpuratam sanctitatem, Sacras decet Violas Magni Myrae recolat.
blocks.english: Shining purity and purple-clad holiness befit sacred violets [the printed concluding Magni Myrae recolat construction is uncertain].
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints Magni Myrae recolat; the relation to the surrounding violets and Nicholas is uncertain. English leaves the concluding construction explicitly unresolved.

blocks.source: Pia tibi mens probetur Dive, esto superetur Labii inopia Laudandorum copia.
blocks.english: May my devout mind be approved by thee, holy one, even though the poverty of my lips is surpassed by the abundance of things to be praised.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed esto superetur is defective; English provisionally follows the abundance of praise surpassing the poverty of speech.

blocks.source: Antiphona (Ps. 21)
blocks.english: Antiphon (Ps. 21)

blocks.source: Apud Te laus mea in Ecclesia magna: Vota mea reddam in conspectu timentium Eum.
blocks.english: With Thee is my praise in the great church; I shall fulfil my vows in the sight of those who fear Him.

blocks.source: ℣. Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore.
blocks.english: ℣. I shall bless the Lord at all times.

blocks.source: ℟. Semper laus ejus in ore meo. (Ps. 33) Oremus,
blocks.english: ℟. His praise is always in my mouth. (Ps. 33) Let us pray.

blocks.source: Exaudi quaesumus Domine preces nostras, quas in Beati Nicolai Confessoris tui atque Pontificis solemnitate deferimus: et qui Tibi digne meruit famulari, ejus intercedentibus meritis, ab omnibus nos absolve peccatis. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Hear, we beseech Thee, Lord, our prayers which we bring on the solemnity of blessed Nicholas Thy Confessor and Bishop; and by the intercession of the merits of him who deserved to serve Thee worthily, absolve us from all sins. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, Who liveth and reigneth with Thee in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Vix illustri stirpe fatum, Jam ad magna videt natum Tanto cive patria Celebris Bononia.
blocks.english: Scarcely born of illustrious stock, he is already seen to be born for great things by his homeland, Bologna, renowned for so great a citizen.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints fatum. English provisionally follows the evident birth imagery, without changing the printed form.

blocks.source: Primum florem juventutis (ut, quam ferax est virtutis, esset et scientiae) Dat juris prudentiae.
blocks.english: He gives the first flower of his youth to jurisprudence, that it may be as fruitful in learning as it is in virtue.

blocks.source: Sed ad summa destinatus, Res, spes mundi aversatus Fugit fasces Curiae, Sacrat se Carthusiae.
blocks.english: But destined for the highest things, turning away from the affairs and hopes of the world, he flees the insignia of the court and consecrates himself to the Charterhouse.

blocks.source: O beata solitudo, Sola es beatitudo! Istud Dive capiam, Ut vel sero sapiam.
blocks.english: O blessed solitude, thou alone art blessedness! Holy one, may I grasp this, that I may grow wise even late.

blocks.source: Antiphona (Eccles. 2, 6)
blocks.english: Antiphon (Eccles. 2:6)

blocks.source: Vidi in omnibus vanitatem et afflictionem animi, et nihil permanere sub sole.
blocks.english: I saw vanity and affliction of mind in all things, and that nothing remains beneath the sun.

blocks.source: ℣. Beatus est vir, cujus est nomen Domini spes ejus.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed is the man whose hope is the name of the Lord,

blocks.source: ℟. Et non respexit in vanitates et insanias falsas. (Ps. 39)
blocks.english: ℟. And who has not regarded vanities and false follies. (Ps. 39)

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed direction repeats this office’s full Matins collect; the Let us pray incipit is included in the Matins response.

blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Quanto quaerit plus latere, Urbi tanto resplendere Coeperit virtus rarior, Lux ab umbra clarior.
blocks.english: The more he seeks to remain hidden, the more his rare virtue begins to shine before the city: light made brighter by shadow.

blocks.source: Quam ut Roma coronaret, Quo sic latius micaret, Linqui jubet cellulam, Patriae dat Insulam.
blocks.english: To crown this virtue and let it shine more widely, Rome bids him leave his cell and gives his homeland an island [the PDF prints Insulam, an uncertain word in this context].
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF itself prints Insulam, island, where the appointment imagery would suggest a different word. English retains and marks island rather than silently substituting a mitre.

blocks.source: Tantum nacta Urbs Pastorem, Novum induit decorem, Exul redit Sanctitas, Exultat improbitas.
blocks.english: Having obtained so great a shepherd, the city puts on new beauty. Exiled holiness returns; wickedness rejoices. [The PDF prints Exultat improbitas.]
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints Exultat improbitas, wickedness rejoices. This unusual statement is retained and explicitly identified rather than changed to an assumed intended verb.

blocks.source: Mihi, Dive, fac viliscam, Et ignotus delitescam, Sanctitate inclytus, Soli Deo cognitus.
blocks.english: Holy one, grant that I may be lowly in my own eyes and hide unknown, illustrious in holiness and known to God alone.

blocks.source: Antiphona (Agg. 2)
blocks.english: Antiphon (Agg. 2)

blocks.source: Assumam te Zorobabel serve meus, et ponam te quasi signaculum, quia te elegi.
blocks.english: I shall take thee, Zorobabel My servant, and make thee as a signet, for I have chosen thee.

blocks.source: ℣. Caput in tribubus Israel factus es.
blocks.english: ℣. Thou wast made head among the tribes of Israel,

blocks.source: ℟. Cum parvulus esses in oculis tuis. (1 Reg. 15)
blocks.english: ℟. When thou wast little in thine own eyes. (1 Reg. 15)

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed direction repeats this office’s full Matins collect; the Let us pray incipit is included in the Matins response.

blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Vix haec Viola florescit, Jam in purpuram rubescit; Unius Bononiae Cardo fit Ecclesiae.
blocks.english: Scarcely does this violet bloom when it already reddens into purple; from Bologna alone he becomes a cardinal of the Church.

blocks.source: Purpuratus nil rigoris Vitae minuit prioris, In se inclementior, Quanto eminentior.
blocks.english: Clothed in purple, he diminishes none of the rigour of his former life, the more severe towards himself the more eminent he becomes.

blocks.source: Sic spinosa Christi Ducis Cardinalis Sanctae Crucis Scandit per vestigia Nominis fastigia.
blocks.english: Thus, following the thorny footsteps of Christ his Leader, the Cardinal of the Holy Cross climbs the heights of his name.

blocks.source: Nicolae, non honores Incorruptos mutent mores, Christianus nomine, Sim, et ipso omine.
blocks.english: Nicholas, may honours not alter uncorrupted ways; may I be Christian in name and also in the meaning of that name.

blocks.source: Antiphona (Gal. 6)
blocks.english: Antiphon (Gal. 6)

blocks.source: Mihi autem absit gloriari nisi in Cruce Domini nostri Jesu Christi.
blocks.english: But far be it from me to glory except in the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.

blocks.source: ℣. Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus. (Cant. 5)
blocks.english: ℣. My beloved is white and ruddy. (Cant. 5)

blocks.source: ℟. Qui pascitur inter Lilia. (Cant. 2)
blocks.english: ℟. He feeds among the lilies. (Cant. 2)

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed direction repeats this office’s full Matins collect; the Let us pray incipit is included in the Matins response.

blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Sic in se pie crudelis Curat populi fidelis Leni manu vulnera, Matris gestans viscera.
blocks.english: Thus devoutly severe towards himself, he tends the wounds of the faithful people with a gentle hand, bearing a mother’s compassion.

blocks.source: Adgemiscit ingementi, Pronus solvit poenitenti Peccatorum vincula, Abolet piacula.
blocks.english: He groans with the groaning one, readily loosens the bonds of sins for the penitent, and removes offences.

blocks.source: Hinc ut orbi mederetur Aegrienti, Magnus detur Poenitentiarius, Christi vult Vicarius.
blocks.english: Hence, to heal the ailing world, the Vicar of Christ wills that he be appointed Grand Penitentiary.

blocks.source: Pro me Deum deprecare, Ut peccanti salutare Donum poenitentiae Det, et indulgentiae.
blocks.english: Pray to God for me, that He may give me, a sinner, the saving gift of repentance and indulgence.

blocks.source: Antiphona (Jerem. 1)
blocks.english: Antiphon (Jerem. 1)

blocks.source: Constitui te hodie super gentes, et regna, ut evellas et destruas, et disperdas, et dissipas, et aedifices, et plantes.
blocks.english: Today I have set thee over nations and kingdoms, to root out and destroy, to scatter and disperse, and to build and plant.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed dissipas has a different verbal form from the parallel subjunctives. English provisionally follows the shared commission to scatter and build.

blocks.source: ℣. Inveni Filium Jesse virum secundum cor meum.
blocks.english: ℣. I have found the son of Jesse, a man according to My heart,

blocks.source: ℟. Qui fecit omnes voluntates meas. (Act. 13)
blocks.english: ℟. Who did all My wishes. (Act. 13)

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed direction repeats this office’s full Matins collect; the Let us pray incipit is included in the Matins response.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Apostolicus Legatus Turbidos regnorum status Integrat oraculis, Roborat miraculis.
blocks.english: As apostolic legate he restores the troubled states of kingdoms by his words and strengthens them by miracles.

blocks.source: Pacis studio Togatus, Aulis Principum sagatus Fert de Marte Lauream, Plantat Pacis Oleam.
blocks.english: Clad in the toga through zeal for peace, and in military dress in the courts of princes, he carries the laurel away from war and plants the olive of peace.

blocks.source: Obstupescunt Orbis partes Rem gerendi sacras artes, Approbant Concilia Angeli Consilia.
blocks.english: The regions of the world marvel at his sacred arts of conducting affairs; councils approve the counsels of an angel.

blocks.source: Nostros Dive, terge luctus, Dulces Pacis posse fructus! Cordaque discordia Uniat Concordia!
blocks.english: Holy one, wipe away our griefs [the printed Dulces Pacis posse fructus is defective]. May concord unite discordant hearts!
blocks.editorialNote: The printed Dulces Pacis posse fructus has no secure complete construction. English explicitly leaves this clause unresolved.

blocks.source: Antiphona (Jerem. 28)
blocks.english: Antiphon (Jerem. 28)

blocks.source: Quaerite pacem Civitatis, ad quam transmigrare vos feci, et orate pro ea ad Deum: quia in pace illius erit Pax vobis.
blocks.english: Seek the peace of the city to which I caused you to be carried away, and pray to God for it; for in its peace you shall have peace.

blocks.source: ℣. In doctrina glorificate Dominum. (Jerem. 24)
blocks.english: ℣. Glorify the Lord in teaching. (Jerem. 24)

blocks.source: ℟. Et docete eos servare omnia, quae praecepi vobis. (Matth. 28)
blocks.english: ℟. And teach them to observe all things that I have commanded you. (Matth. 28)

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed direction repeats this office’s full Matins collect; the Let us pray incipit is included in the Matins response.

blocks.source: ℣. Converte nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Sic dum Deo militat, Ad promissum evolavit Praemium militiae: Lauream justitiae.
blocks.english: Thus while serving God as a soldier, he flew to the promised reward of his service: the laurel of justice.

blocks.source: In amoris argumentum Pietatis monumentum Sacrae, vult, Exuviae Cederent Carthusiae.
blocks.english: As proof of love and a memorial of sacred piety, he wishes his mortal remains to be given to the Charterhouse.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed vult, Exuviae Cederent has defective syntax. English provisionally follows the clear wish about the sacred remains and Charterhouse.

blocks.source: Sic cui cella est viventi, Caelum, decet, quiescenti. Mollem sternat lectulum Gloriae in cumulum.
blocks.english: Thus the cell which is heaven to him while living should spread a soft bed for him at rest, to the increase of glory.

blocks.source: O si detur morte pari Fungi, tibi sociari In supernis aedibus, Beatorum sedibus.
blocks.english: O that I may be granted to meet a like death and be joined to thee in heavenly dwellings, the seats of the blessed!

blocks.source: Antiphona (2 Cor. 5)
blocks.english: Antiphon. 2 Corinthians 5.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from a reviewed passage elsewhere in this PDF with the same complete sequence of Latin words and numbers. Only punctuation and capitalization differ; the target Latin is retained. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Scimus quoniam si terrestris domus nostra hujus habitationis dissolvatur, quod aedificationem ex Deo habemus, domum non manufactam in caelis.
blocks.english: We know that if this earthly house of our dwelling is dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made by hands in heaven.

blocks.source: ℣. Pretiosa in conspectu Domini. (Ps. 115)
blocks.english: ℣. Precious in the sight of the Lord. (Ps. 115)

blocks.source: ℟. Mors Sanctorum ejus.
blocks.english: ℟. Is the death of His saints.
blocks.editorialNote: English reused from an identical complete Latin passage elsewhere in this PDF. This office’s source transcription still requires its own review.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed direction repeats this office’s full Matins collect; the Let us pray incipit is included in the Matins response.

blocks.source: Gloriose Coeli Civis! Tuum sentiam ubivis! Fave! Patrocinium, Validum Praesidium!
blocks.english: Glorious citizen of heaven, may I feel thy patronage everywhere. Favour me with thy mighty protection!

blocks.source: Rege linguam, aures, tactum, Rege gustum, et olfactum, Vagos Rege oculos, Animorum scopulos.
blocks.english: Govern my tongue, ears, and touch; govern taste and smell; govern my wandering eyes, the rocks upon which souls founder.

blocks.source: Vincam carnis blandimenta, Vana daemonis figmenta Ludam, et fallacias; Spernam mundi gratias.
blocks.english: May I conquer the enticements of the flesh, mock the vain inventions and deceits of the demon, and scorn the favours of the world.

blocks.source: Aegrienti Archiaeter, Poenitenti esto Pater, Dissidentem erige, Praesidentem corrige.
blocks.english: Be chief physician to the sick and father to the penitent; raise the one who dissents and correct the one who presides.

blocks.source: Da virtutes imitari, Pretiosa aemulari Sanctitatis dogmata, Gratiae Charismata.
blocks.english: Grant me to imitate virtues and emulate the precious teachings of holiness and gifts of grace.

editorialNotes.text: Prepared English was compared visually with PDF pages 569–572. All seven printed hours and the five-stanza commendation remain; no Lauds is added. Repeated collect directions expand within this office. Printed Insulam and Exultat improbitas are retained and explained; defective hymn clauses remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. Source reading is pending.
